recommendation: Keep this source-changing commit as-is. It applies the published clarification narrowly, preserves Binary-specific behavior, and avoids changing unrelated content negotiation requirements.
issue_request: FHIR-13186 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-core HTTP change request asking the mime-type section to clarify whether clients may send an Accept header of */*. The approved resolution was to document that servers are encouraged to support it and return JSON or XML at their discretion.
initial_application: No source/http.html commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-13186 was found. The page contained related generic Accept-header guidance from #10200/FHIR-9029 and the later FHIR-25200 correction, but it did not mention */* before this reconciliation.
additional_context: source/http.html is the tracked top-level source for the HTTP page and the Jira related http.html#mime-type section. Later history maintained two parallel generic Accept-header notes on this page, so both locations needed the wildcard clarification. Zulip and Confluence searches found no directly relevant discussion that narrowed or reversed the Jira resolution.
reconciliation: Updated source/http.html in the Content Types and encodings implementation notes and the matching _format/return-content implementation notes to state that non-Binary resources SHOULD support Accept: */* and may choose JSON or XML for the response at their discretion.
source_changes: source/http.html: added wildcard Accept guidance in the Content Types and encodings implementation notes.
source/http.html: added the same wildcard Accept guidance in the matching _format/return-content implementation notes.
